scope: Proposition 15.5 (Spatial product kernels) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 186. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every open coordinate domain U, the collection of all certificates with compact range in U has a regular conditional law KU (h|U , b h|U ; ·) depending only on the restrictions of the two fields to U. If U1, . . . , Um are disjoint open sets, these collections are conditionally independent given the complete fields, with respective conditional laws KUi . These laws are consistent under restriction and exhaustion. They also exist on the free-field patches obtained by local absolute continuity in Proposition 13.4. Here the local collection retains projected endpoints and ranges, costs, and ordered-subpath incidences; the original global contour-time labels have been forgotten. Relative parametrizations inside locally retained cells may be used during the construction. In particular one can preserve a sampled collection on each of finitely many disjoint patches and complete it to a sample of the whole certificate law, provided that the preserved collections have the specified product conditional law for the new fields on those patches. This statement concerns conditional sampling; it makes no assertion that the competitor satisfies a Weyl rule.
